1. SCOPE: Estimand: mean baseline biomarker value (ng/mL) across all patients. Population: all patients in trial, one row per patient. Units: ng/mL.

The analyst deduplicated on patient_id keeping highest sample_seq, which matches data dictionary: each patient may have multiple rows, keep highest. Then excluded -999 sentinel. That yields 712 patients. This matches "all patients" after handling duplicates and missing sentinel. So scope is appropriate.

3. OVERREACH: No causal claim, just descriptive mean. No overreach.

4. UNACKNOWLEDGED DATA PROBLEMS: Are there any issues not addressed? The data dictionary mentions assay_batch unit error only for biomarker_final, not baseline, so fine. They didn't address potential bias due to missing -999 values (maybe not missing at random). But they did note sentinel removal. The contract didn't require addressing missingness bias. The output shows no other problems. The duplicate handling is correct per dictionary. So no unacknowledged problems.

Thus answer is sound.
